rule: Every symbol is a real record: a public court record, published works (title, author line and year only, never the text), a published PGP key fingerprint, dated forum posts and real block heights. The people appear only as Jim's own pop-art prints (see 'prints'), never as photographs, and nobody is named as Satoshi.

cherry.kind: Public court record, shown as Jim's prints of the case (COPA v Wright, Mr Justice Mellor) and a typed case-file card
cherry.record: COPA v Wright [2024] EWHC 1198 (Ch), Mr Justice Mellor, written judgment 20 May 2024; declaration 14 March 2024
wording: Found: not the author of the Bitcoin White Paper
Found: documents forged "on a grand scale"

wild.name: The Whitepaper
wild.kind: Historic document with Satoshi's print (a hood and ₿, no face)
wild.record: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, Satoshi Nakamoto, 31 October 2008

scatter.name: Forum post
scatter.note: 15 short, widely quoted lines with dates, from the Satoshi Nakamoto Institute archive (dates as the archive gives them).

items.text: No mint or other trusted parties.
It's very attractive to the libertarian viewpoint if we can explain it properly.
I'm better with code than with words though.
It's completely decentralized with no server or central authority.
It might make sense just to get some in case it catches on.
The root problem with conventional currency is all the trust that's required to make it work.
How does everyone feel about the B symbol with the two lines through the outside?
Much more of the work was designing than coding.
Lost coins only make everyone else's coins worth slightly more.
Writing a description for this thing for general audiences is bloody hard.
Escape the arbitrary inflation risk of centrally managed currencies!
More like a collectible or commodity.
Bitcoin is a small beta community in its infancy.

logosNote: No other project's logo appears on this machine. The only marks are the house marks (Xtrata, ParallaX Casino) and the public-domain ₿ glyph.
openQuestions: The Forgery wording follows the judgment as reported (bible open question: confirm you are happy with it).

The key fingerprint was taken from the Bitcoin Foundation bylaws on GitHub because the Internet Archive and bitcoin.org copies of Satoshi_Nakamoto.asc could not be fetched from the build machine; compare against the archived key before launch.

Real people now appear on the reels as Jim's prints. Szabo, Back and Dai have publicly denied being Satoshi, and the Wright print sits on the Forgery symbol with a NOT SATOSHI stamp; worth a check before the machine goes on the public floor.

prints.madeBy: Jim (jim.btc), ParallaX Casino: his own pop-art prints, supplied as one 4x4 grid on 2 Nov 2026 (art/prints/source-grid.jpg) and cut into 16 tiles of 240 px
prints.note: No photograph of anyone is used in the game; these prints are the only images of people.
